We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. **Michael James Radford** (born 24 February 1946) is an English film director and screenwriter.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT-1) He began his career as a documentary director and television comedy writer before transitioning into features in the early 1980s.

His best-known credits include the 1984 [film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen_Eighty-Four_(1984_film) "Nineteen Eighty-Four (1984 film)") of [George Orwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Orwell "George Orwell")'s _[Nineteen Eighty-Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen\_Eighty-Four "Nineteen Eighty-Four")_ starring [John Hurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hurt "John Hurt") and [Richard Burton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Burton "Richard Burton") (in his final role), the [Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare") adaptation _[The Merchant of Venice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Merchant\_of\_Venice\_(2004\_film) "The Merchant of Venice (2004 film)")_, the [true crime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/True_crime "True crime") drama _[White Mischief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White\_Mischief\_(film) "White Mischief (film)")_, and the 1994 Italian-language comedy drama _[Il Postino: The Postman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Il\_Postino:\_The\_Postman "Il Postino: The Postman")_, for which he won the [BAFTA Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Awards "BAFTA Awards") for [Best Direction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Direction "BAFTA Award for Best Direction") and [Best Film Not in the English Language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Film_Not_in_the_English_Language "BAFTA Award for Best Film Not in the English Language"), and earned [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") nominations for [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Director "Academy Award for Best Director") and [Best Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Adapted_Screenplay "Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay").

## Early life and career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Radford&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and career")]

Radford was born on 24 February 1946, in [New Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi "New Delhi"), [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidencies_and_provinces_of_British_India "Presidencies and provinces of British India"), to a British father and an Austrian [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish "Jewish") mother. He was educated at [Bedford School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bedford_School "Bedford School") before attending [Worcester College, Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worcester_College,_Oxford "Worcester College, Oxford"). After teaching for a few years, he went to the [National Film and Television School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_and_Television_School "National Film and Television School"), becoming a student there in its inaugural year.

Between 1976 and 1982, Radford worked as a documentary film maker, mostly on projects for the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC"), covering subjects such as Scottish islanders on the [Isle of Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isle_of_Lewis "Isle of Lewis") in the [Outer Hebrides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outer_Hebrides "Outer Hebrides") who believe in the literal truth of the Bible: _The Last Stronghold of the Pure Gospel_; the soprano [Isobel Buchanan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isobel_Buchanan "Isobel Buchanan"): _La Belle Isobel_; the singer songwriter [Van Morrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Morrison "Van Morrison"): _[Van Morrison in Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van\_Morrison\_in\_Ireland "Van Morrison in Ireland")_; and the self-explanatory _The Making of [The Pirates of Penzance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Pirates\_of\_Penzance "The Pirates of Penzance")_. On the last two of these, Radford worked with the [cinematographer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinematographer "Cinematographer")[Roger Deakins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Deakins "Roger Deakins"), who would later shoot two of Radford's feature films; _[Nineteen Eighty-Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen\_Eighty-Four\_(1984\_film) "Nineteen Eighty-Four (1984 film)")_ and _[White Mischief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White\_Mischief\_(film) "White Mischief (film)")_. Another notable early work was _[Another Time, Another Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another\_Time,\_Another\_Place\_(1983\_film) "Another Time, Another Place (1983 film)")_ (1983), a feature film set in [Scotland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scotland "Scotland") during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") and centred on a love story between a local woman and an [Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy")[POW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prisoner_of_war "Prisoner of war").

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Radford&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Radford came to international attention with _[Nineteen Eighty-Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen\_Eighty-Four\_(1984\_film) "Nineteen Eighty-Four (1984 film)")_, his adaptation of [George Orwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Orwell "George Orwell")'s novel _[1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen\_Eighty-Four "Nineteen Eighty-Four")_, starring [John Hurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hurt "John Hurt") as Winston Smith, and in which [Richard Burton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Burton "Richard Burton") gave his final film performance.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) The film was made in the time and place ([London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), April–June 1984) at which the book was set.

Radford's next film, released in 1987, was _[White Mischief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White\_Mischief\_(film) "White Mischief (film)")_, a period drama set in [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") during the 1940s.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) Radford again wrote the screenplay, an adaptation of the novel by [James Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox_(journalist) "James Fox (journalist)") also called _White Mischief_.

Michael Radford is most widely known as the writer and director of the 1994 film _[Il Postino: The Postman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Il\_Postino:\_The\_Postman "Il Postino: The Postman")_, which Radford adapted from the novel _[Ardiente Paciencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardiente\_paciencia "Ardiente paciencia")_ by [Antonio Skármeta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Sk%C3%A1rmeta "Antonio Skármeta").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT-1) The massive international success of the film (for many years it was the largest grossing non-English language film ever made) led to international acclaim for Radford and the star of the film [Massimo Troisi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massimo_Troisi "Massimo Troisi"). Tragically, Troisi died, aged 41, the day after the filming of _Il Postino_ was completed. The film won many international film awards including the 'Best Film Not in the English Language' [BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_of_Film_and_Television_Arts "British Academy of Film and Television Arts") for Radford, who was also nominated for the [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Director "Academy Award for Best Director") and [Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Writing_Adapted_Screenplay "Academy Award for Writing Adapted Screenplay")[Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards").

In 2000, Radford's film _[Dancing at the Blue Iguana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancing\_at\_the\_Blue\_Iguana "Dancing at the Blue Iguana")_ was released.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) In a departure from his more usual development technique, namely adapting novels, this film was largely improvised, although Radford shared the screenwriting credit with [David Linter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Linter?action=edit&redlink=1 "David Linter (page does not exist)").

In 2004, Radford directed _[The Merchant of Venice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Merchant\_of\_Venice\_(2004\_film) "The Merchant of Venice (2004 film)")_ (2004).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) He adapted the [William Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare") play (see: [Shakespearean comedies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakespearean_comedies "Shakespearean comedies")), and the film stars [Al Pacino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Pacino "Al Pacino") as [Shylock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shylock "Shylock") and [Jeremy Irons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Irons "Jeremy Irons") as [Antonio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_(Merchant_of_Venice) "Antonio (Merchant of Venice)").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) In 2007, he reunited [Demi Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demi_Moore "Demi Moore") and [Michael Caine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Caine "Michael Caine") (who had already been together in 1984 for _[Blame it on Rio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blame\_it\_on\_Rio "Blame it on Rio")_) in _[Flawless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flawless\_(2007\_film) "Flawless (2007 film)")_, a diamond heist story set in 1960.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) His most recent film is _[Elsa & Fred](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elsa\_&\_Fred\_(2014\_film) "Elsa & Fred (2014 film)")_ (2014), a romantic comedy starring [Shirley MacLaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shirley_MacLaine "Shirley MacLaine") and [Christopher Plummer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Plummer "Christopher Plummer").

Radford directed his first play in 2000, a [West End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_End_theatre "West End theatre") production of _[The Seven Year Itch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Seven\_Year\_Itch "The Seven Year Itch")_. This was an adaptation of [Billy Wilder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Wilder "Billy Wilder")'s 1955 film starring [Marilyn Monroe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marilyn_Monroe "Marilyn Monroe").

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Radford&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Radford has a son, Felix (born 1991), from his first marriage to Iseult Teran. He also has a daughter, Amaryllis (born 2005), and a son, Linus (born 2010), with his current wife, Emma Tweed.

In addition to English (his first language), he speaks fluent Spanish, French, Italian, and some Mandarin.

In September 2013, he took part in the Clipper Round the World Sailing Race, in which he raced one of 12 identical 70-foot racing yachts from London to Rio.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-3)

**Michael James Radford** (born 24 February 1946) is an English film director and screenwriter.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT-1) He began his career as a documentary director and television comedy writer before transitioning into features in the early 1980s.

His best-known credits include the 1984 [film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen_Eighty-Four_(1984_film) "Nineteen Eighty-Four (1984 film)") of [George Orwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Orwell "George Orwell")'s _[Nineteen Eighty-Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen\_Eighty-Four "Nineteen Eighty-Four")_ starring [John Hurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hurt "John Hurt") and [Richard Burton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Burton "Richard Burton") (in his final role), the [Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare") adaptation _[The Merchant of Venice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Merchant\_of\_Venice\_(2004\_film) "The Merchant of Venice (2004 film)")_, the [true crime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/True_crime "True crime") drama _[White Mischief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White\_Mischief\_(film) "White Mischief (film)")_, and the 1994 Italian-language comedy drama _[Il Postino: The Postman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Il\_Postino:\_The\_Postman "Il Postino: The Postman")_, for which he won the [BAFTA Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Awards "BAFTA Awards") for [Best Direction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Direction "BAFTA Award for Best Direction") and [Best Film Not in the English Language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Film_Not_in_the_English_Language "BAFTA Award for Best Film Not in the English Language"), and earned [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") nominations for [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Director "Academy Award for Best Director") and [Best Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Adapted_Screenplay "Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay").

## Early life and career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Radford&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and career")]

Radford was born on 24 February 1946, in [New Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi "New Delhi"), [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidencies_and_provinces_of_British_India "Presidencies and provinces of British India"), to a British father and an Austrian [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish "Jewish") mother. He was educated at [Bedford School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bedford_School "Bedford School") before attending [Worcester College, Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worcester_College,_Oxford "Worcester College, Oxford"). After teaching for a few years, he went to the [National Film and Television School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_and_Television_School "National Film and Television School"), becoming a student there in its inaugural year.

Between 1976 and 1982, Radford worked as a documentary film maker, mostly on projects for the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC"), covering subjects such as Scottish islanders on the [Isle of Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isle_of_Lewis "Isle of Lewis") in the [Outer Hebrides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outer_Hebrides "Outer Hebrides") who believe in the literal truth of the Bible: _The Last Stronghold of the Pure Gospel_; the soprano [Isobel Buchanan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isobel_Buchanan "Isobel Buchanan"): _La Belle Isobel_; the singer songwriter [Van Morrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Morrison "Van Morrison"): _[Van Morrison in Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van\_Morrison\_in\_Ireland "Van Morrison in Ireland")_; and the self-explanatory _The Making of [The Pirates of Penzance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Pirates\_of\_Penzance "The Pirates of Penzance")_. On the last two of these, Radford worked with the [cinematographer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinematographer "Cinematographer")[Roger Deakins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Deakins "Roger Deakins"), who would later shoot two of Radford's feature films; _[Nineteen Eighty-Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen\_Eighty-Four\_(1984\_film) "Nineteen Eighty-Four (1984 film)")_ and _[White Mischief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White\_Mischief\_(film) "White Mischief (film)")_. Another notable early work was _[Another Time, Another Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another\_Time,\_Another\_Place\_(1983\_film) "Another Time, Another Place (1983 film)")_ (1983), a feature film set in [Scotland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scotland "Scotland") during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") and centred on a love story between a local woman and an [Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy")[POW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prisoner_of_war "Prisoner of war").

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Radford&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Radford came to international attention with _[Nineteen Eighty-Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen\_Eighty-Four\_(1984\_film) "Nineteen Eighty-Four (1984 film)")_, his adaptation of [George Orwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Orwell "George Orwell")'s novel _[1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen\_Eighty-Four "Nineteen Eighty-Four")_, starring [John Hurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hurt "John Hurt") as Winston Smith, and in which [Richard Burton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Burton "Richard Burton") gave his final film performance.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) The film was made in the time and place ([London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), April–June 1984) at which the book was set.

Radford's next film, released in 1987, was _[White Mischief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White\_Mischief\_(film) "White Mischief (film)")_, a period drama set in [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") during the 1940s.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) Radford again wrote the screenplay, an adaptation of the novel by [James Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox_(journalist) "James Fox (journalist)") also called _White Mischief_.

Michael Radford is most widely known as the writer and director of the 1994 film _[Il Postino: The Postman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Il\_Postino:\_The\_Postman "Il Postino: The Postman")_, which Radford adapted from the novel _[Ardiente Paciencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardiente\_paciencia "Ardiente paciencia")_ by [Antonio Skármeta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Sk%C3%A1rmeta "Antonio Skármeta").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT-1) The massive international success of the film (for many years it was the largest grossing non-English language film ever made) led to international acclaim for Radford and the star of the film [Massimo Troisi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massimo_Troisi "Massimo Troisi"). Tragically, Troisi died, aged 41, the day after the filming of _Il Postino_ was completed. The film won many international film awards including the 'Best Film Not in the English Language' [BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_of_Film_and_Television_Arts "British Academy of Film and Television Arts") for Radford, who was also nominated for the [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Director "Academy Award for Best Director") and [Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Writing_Adapted_Screenplay "Academy Award for Writing Adapted Screenplay")[Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards").

In 2000, Radford's film _[Dancing at the Blue Iguana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancing\_at\_the\_Blue\_Iguana "Dancing at the Blue Iguana")_ was released.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) In a departure from his more usual development technique, namely adapting novels, this film was largely improvised, although Radford shared the screenwriting credit with [David Linter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Linter?action=edit&redlink=1 "David Linter (page does not exist)").

In 2004, Radford directed _[The Merchant of Venice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Merchant\_of\_Venice\_(2004\_film) "The Merchant of Venice (2004 film)")_ (2004).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) He adapted the [William Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare") play (see: [Shakespearean comedies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakespearean_comedies "Shakespearean comedies")), and the film stars [Al Pacino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Pacino "Al Pacino") as [Shylock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shylock "Shylock") and [Jeremy Irons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Irons "Jeremy Irons") as [Antonio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_(Merchant_of_Venice) "Antonio (Merchant of Venice)").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) In 2007, he reunited [Demi Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demi_Moore "Demi Moore") and [Michael Caine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Caine "Michael Caine") (who had already been together in 1984 for _[Blame it on Rio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blame\_it\_on\_Rio "Blame it on Rio")_) in _[Flawless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flawless\_(2007\_film) "Flawless (2007 film)")_, a diamond heist story set in 1960.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) His most recent film is _[Elsa & Fred](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elsa\_&\_Fred\_(2014\_film) "Elsa & Fred (2014 film)")_ (2014), a romantic comedy starring [Shirley MacLaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shirley_MacLaine "Shirley MacLaine") and [Christopher Plummer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Plummer "Christopher Plummer").

Radford directed his first play in 2000, a [West End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_End_theatre "West End theatre") production of _[The Seven Year Itch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Seven\_Year\_Itch "The Seven Year Itch")_. This was an adaptation of [Billy Wilder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Wilder "Billy Wilder")'s 1955 film starring [Marilyn Monroe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marilyn_Monroe "Marilyn Monroe").

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Radford&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Radford has a son, Felix (born 1991), from his first marriage to Iseult Teran. He also has a daughter, Amaryllis (born 2005), and a son, Linus (born 2010), with his current wife, Emma Tweed.

In addition to English (his first language), he speaks fluent Spanish, French, Italian, and some Mandarin.

In September 2013, he took part in the Clipper Round the World Sailing Race, in which he raced one of 12 identical 70-foot racing yachts from London to Rio.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-3)

_**White Mischief**_ is a 1987 British [period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_drama "Historical drama")[crime drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_drama "Crime drama") film directed and co-written by Michael Radford. It dramatises the events of the [Happy Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happy_Valley_set "Happy Valley set") murder case in [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") in 1941, wherein Sir [Henry “Jock” Delves Broughton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jock_Delves_Broughton "Jock Delves Broughton") was tried for the murder of [Josslyn Hay, 22nd Earl of Erroll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josslyn_Hay,_22nd_Earl_of_Erroll "Josslyn Hay, 22nd Earl of Erroll"). The film stars [Greta Scacchi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greta_Scacchi "Greta Scacchi"), [Charles Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Dance "Charles Dance"), [Joss Ackland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland "Joss Ackland"), [Sarah Miles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Miles "Sarah Miles"), [Geraldine Chaplin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geraldine_Chaplin "Geraldine Chaplin"), [Ray McAnally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_McAnally "Ray McAnally"), [Murray Head](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murray_Head "Murray Head"), [John Hurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hurt "John Hurt"), and [Trevor Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Howard "Trevor Howard").

The screenplay is based on the non-fiction book _[White Mischief: The Murder of Lord Erroll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White\_Mischief\_(novel) "White Mischief (novel)")_ (1982), by [James Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox_(journalist) "James Fox (journalist)"), which originated from a newspaper article published in 1969.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-whitemischief-6) Shooting took place on-location in Kenya and at [Shepperton Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shepperton_Studios "Shepperton Studios").

At the [42nd British Academy Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/42nd_British_Academy_Film_Awards "42nd British Academy Film Awards"), the film was nominated for [Best Actor in a Supporting Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Supporting_Role "BAFTA Award for Best Actor in a Supporting Role") (for Joss Ackland) and [Best Costume Design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Costume_Design "BAFTA Award for Best Costume Design").

The film came out around the same time as a BBC series set against the background of the same crime, _[The Happy Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Happy\_Valley "The Happy Valley")_ (1987).

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

Throughout the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), aristocrats in the [Kenya Colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Colony "Kenya Colony")'s Happy Valley region often led hedonistic lifestyles of indulgence in alcohol, drugs, and extramarital relationships. On 24 January 1941, Josslyn Hay, the philandering Earl of Erroll, was found dead in his car in a secluded area, with his reputation for adulterous relationships preceding him.

One such married woman is [Diana Delves Broughton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diana_Caldwell "Diana Caldwell"), the beautiful wife of Sir John Henry Delves Broughton, known as "Jock", who is thirty years her senior, with whom she has a pre-nuptial understanding that, should either of them fall in love with someone else, the other party would not impede that romance.

Diana has indeed succumbed to the charms of the Earl of Erroll,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-jongh-7) whose other lovers include the drug-addicted American heiress [Alice de Janzé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_de_Janz%C3%A9 "Alice de Janzé") and the more reserved Nina Soames. The Earl is more serious about this affair than any of his earlier dalliances, and wants Diana to marry him. She is reluctant to leave what she thinks is the financial security of her marriage to formalise her relationship with Erroll (who has no funds or prospects), unaware that her husband is deep in debt. Privately humiliated but appearing to honour their agreement, Delves Broughton publicly toasts the couple's affair at the club in Nairobi, asking Erroll to bring Diana home at a specified time. Delves Broughton appears to be extremely intoxicated for the rest of the evening; once he is alone it is clear he was feigning drunkenness. After dropping off Diana, Erroll is shot dead in his car near the home of Delves Broughton, who is soon charged with the murder.

Diana is distraught over losing her lover, as is Alice, who openly masturbates next to his corpse at the mortuary. A local plantation owner, Gilbert Colvile, whose only friend is Delves Broughton, quietly offers Diana advice and solace and ultimately shocks her by proposing marriage.

Delves Broughton stands trial. There are no witnesses to the crime and the physical evidence that appears incriminating is also circumstantial. He obviously had the motive and means, but is found innocent, and the scandal comes to an end. De Janzé ultimately kills herself, and Diana discovers further evidence that implicates her husband in her lover's death. After killing their dog and then menacing her with a shotgun, Broughton shoots himself in front of her. The film ends with a fleeing, bloodstained Diana discovering the remaining Happy Valley set partying around de Janzé's grave.

## Original book

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Original book")]

In 1969, James Fox and [Cyril Connolly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyril_Connolly "Cyril Connolly") began investigating the case for an article in _The Sunday Times_ called "Christmas at Karen." After Connolly died in 1974, Fox inherited his notes and theories, and returned to Kenya to undertake further research. The result was the book _White Mischief_, published in 1982.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-8)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-sight-3) The title came from _[Black Mischief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_Mischief "Black Mischief")_, [Evelyn Waugh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evelyn_Waugh "Evelyn Waugh")'s satirical novel set in the mythical African kingdom of Azania. _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ called it "a fascinating book."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-9)_[The Boston Globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Boston\_Globe "The Boston Globe")_ said "had ‘White Mischief’ been a work of fiction it would have required the collaboration of [Agatha Christie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agatha_Christie "Agatha Christie") and [P. G. Wodehouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P._G._Wodehouse "P. G. Wodehouse")."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-10) While researching the book Fox also collected information about [Beryl Markham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beryl_Markham "Beryl Markham"), which was turned into the film _[A Shadow on the Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beryl\_Markham:\_A\_Shadow\_on\_the\_Sun "Beryl Markham: A Shadow on the Sun")_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-11)

## Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Development")]

The film rights to the book were optioned by [Michael White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_White_(producer) "Michael White (producer)"), a friend of Fox's, while the book was being written.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-12)

Director Michael Radford collaborated with British playwright [Jonathan Gems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Gems "Jonathan Gems") on the script. Radford emphasized that "films of [Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa "Africa") should be made by Africans" and described the project as "a film of melancholy about people who have everything and yet have nothing. It's about people who want to possess what they can't possess."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-csm-13)

Securing funding for the film posed a challenge. The financing was sourced from a chain of Canadian cinemas, [Cineplex Odeon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cineplex_Odeon_Corporation "Cineplex Odeon Corporation"), plus [Goldcrest Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldcrest_Films "Goldcrest Films")[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-ink-14), BBC Television, [Nelson Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Entertainment "Nelson Entertainment") (headed by [Barry Spikings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Spikings "Barry Spikings"), which provided $2.5 million in exchange for North American video rights), with the remaining amount coming from [Columbia Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Pictures "Columbia Pictures"), then under [David Puttnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Puttnam "David Puttnam") as head of production.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-white-2)

[Richard Attenborough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Attenborough "Richard Attenborough") was offered and turned down the lead role, because he wanted to focus on directing films.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-15)

## Shooting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Shooting")]

Filming took place from February to May 1987 at [Shepperton Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shepperton_Studios "Shepperton Studios") and on location in Kenya.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-16)[Wrotham Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrotham_Park "Wrotham Park") was used as [Doddington Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doddington_Hall,_Cheshire "Doddington Hall, Cheshire"), the home of Delves Broughton.

## Historical accuracy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Historical accuracy")]

The real Alice De Janzé shot herself on 30 September 1941,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-17) while Jock Delves Broughton eventually returned to England and committed suicide by [morphine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphine "Morphine") overdose in the [Adelphi Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britannia_Adelphi_Hotel "Britannia Adelphi Hotel") in [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool "Liverpool") in December 1942, over a year later.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-18)

"There is a difference between fact and truth," said producer Simon Perry. "You can be truthful without being factual. It's inevitable there will be people who think Kenya was and still is a paradise of [remittance men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remittance_man "Remittance man") and black sheep of aristocratic families. Kenya was an exaggerated microcosm of society in Britain at that time, painted in primary colours with characters larger than life."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-csm-13)

Sir Jock Broughton's son, Sir Evelyn, complained that the film depicted his father as a murderer. He said his father was too drunk that night to have committed the crime and that Diana was more likely to have done it.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-19)

Diana Broughton died in 1987.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-20)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Box office

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Box office")]

The film grossed £1,532,903 in the United Kingdom and $3.1 million in the United States and Canada.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-screen-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-mojo-5) It lost money during its theatrical release, however, [Jake Eberts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Eberts "Jake Eberts") reported that [Goldcrest Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldcrest_Films "Goldcrest Films") invested £1,300,000 in the film, and received £1,633,000, earning them a profit of £333,000.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-screen-4)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-23)

### Critical

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Critical")]

_[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety\_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")_ wrote the film "displays high production values, impressive acting talent, and a strong — virtually factual — storyline. The money invested can be seen on the screen, and with an excellent lead performance (following his major role in ‘‘The Sicilian’’) Joss Ackland should finally receive the acting kudos he deserves. Pic should make a healthy b.o. impact worldwide."[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-24)

Book author James Fox said he was "ambivalent" about the movie.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-jongh-7)

Radford said the reviews of the film " almost ruined my career. It stopped it in its tracks... I think it was difficult for critics because Britain is obsessed by class. It wasn’t done to make a film about upper-class people. I think people were expecting one of those James Ivory films or _A Passage to India_... It wasn’t meant to be like _Out of Africa_, the cinema of waxed furniture. I was trying to make something much more decadent."[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-25)

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Legacy")]

In 1996, [Mariette Bosch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariette_Bosch "Mariette Bosch") murdered Ria Wolmerans in [Botswana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botswana "Botswana"). Both women were white South Africans. The case was referred to as "Botswana's white mischief".[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-BarrowBBC-26)

_**White Mischief**_ is a 1987 British [period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_drama "Historical drama")[crime drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_drama "Crime drama") film directed and co-written by Michael Radford. It dramatises the events of the [Happy Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happy_Valley_set "Happy Valley set") murder case in [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") in 1941, wherein Sir [Henry “Jock” Delves Broughton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jock_Delves_Broughton "Jock Delves Broughton") was tried for the murder of [Josslyn Hay, 22nd Earl of Erroll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josslyn_Hay,_22nd_Earl_of_Erroll "Josslyn Hay, 22nd Earl of Erroll"). The film stars [Greta Scacchi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greta_Scacchi "Greta Scacchi"), [Charles Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Dance "Charles Dance"), [Joss Ackland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland "Joss Ackland"), [Sarah Miles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Miles "Sarah Miles"), [Geraldine Chaplin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geraldine_Chaplin "Geraldine Chaplin"), [Ray McAnally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_McAnally "Ray McAnally"), [Murray Head](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murray_Head "Murray Head"), [John Hurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hurt "John Hurt"), and [Trevor Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Howard "Trevor Howard").

The screenplay is based on the non-fiction book _[White Mischief: The Murder of Lord Erroll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White\_Mischief\_(novel) "White Mischief (novel)")_ (1982), by [James Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox_(journalist) "James Fox (journalist)"), which originated from a newspaper article published in 1969.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-whitemischief-6) Shooting took place on-location in Kenya and at [Shepperton Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shepperton_Studios "Shepperton Studios").

At the [42nd British Academy Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/42nd_British_Academy_Film_Awards "42nd British Academy Film Awards"), the film was nominated for [Best Actor in a Supporting Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Supporting_Role "BAFTA Award for Best Actor in a Supporting Role") (for Joss Ackland) and [Best Costume Design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Costume_Design "BAFTA Award for Best Costume Design").

The film came out around the same time as a BBC series set against the background of the same crime, _[The Happy Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Happy\_Valley "The Happy Valley")_ (1987).

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

Throughout the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), aristocrats in the [Kenya Colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Colony "Kenya Colony")'s Happy Valley region often led hedonistic lifestyles of indulgence in alcohol, drugs, and extramarital relationships. On 24 January 1941, Josslyn Hay, the philandering Earl of Erroll, was found dead in his car in a secluded area, with his reputation for adulterous relationships preceding him.

One such married woman is [Diana Delves Broughton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diana_Caldwell "Diana Caldwell"), the beautiful wife of Sir John Henry Delves Broughton, known as "Jock", who is thirty years her senior, with whom she has a pre-nuptial understanding that, should either of them fall in love with someone else, the other party would not impede that romance.

Diana has indeed succumbed to the charms of the Earl of Erroll,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-jongh-7) whose other lovers include the drug-addicted American heiress [Alice de Janzé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_de_Janz%C3%A9 "Alice de Janzé") and the more reserved Nina Soames. The Earl is more serious about this affair than any of his earlier dalliances, and wants Diana to marry him. She is reluctant to leave what she thinks is the financial security of her marriage to formalise her relationship with Erroll (who has no funds or prospects), unaware that her husband is deep in debt. Privately humiliated but appearing to honour their agreement, Delves Broughton publicly toasts the couple's affair at the club in Nairobi, asking Erroll to bring Diana home at a specified time. Delves Broughton appears to be extremely intoxicated for the rest of the evening; once he is alone it is clear he was feigning drunkenness. After dropping off Diana, Erroll is shot dead in his car near the home of Delves Broughton, who is soon charged with the murder.

Diana is distraught over losing her lover, as is Alice, who openly masturbates next to his corpse at the mortuary. A local plantation owner, Gilbert Colvile, whose only friend is Delves Broughton, quietly offers Diana advice and solace and ultimately shocks her by proposing marriage.

Delves Broughton stands trial. There are no witnesses to the crime and the physical evidence that appears incriminating is also circumstantial. He obviously had the motive and means, but is found innocent, and the scandal comes to an end. De Janzé ultimately kills herself, and Diana discovers further evidence that implicates her husband in her lover's death. After killing their dog and then menacing her with a shotgun, Broughton shoots himself in front of her. The film ends with a fleeing, bloodstained Diana discovering the remaining Happy Valley set partying around de Janzé's grave.

## Original book

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Original book")]

In 1969, James Fox and [Cyril Connolly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyril_Connolly "Cyril Connolly") began investigating the case for an article in _The Sunday Times_ called "Christmas at Karen." After Connolly died in 1974, Fox inherited his notes and theories, and returned to Kenya to undertake further research. The result was the book _White Mischief_, published in 1982.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-8)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-sight-3) The title came from _[Black Mischief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_Mischief "Black Mischief")_, [Evelyn Waugh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evelyn_Waugh "Evelyn Waugh")'s satirical novel set in the mythical African kingdom of Azania. _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ called it "a fascinating book."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-9)_[The Boston Globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Boston\_Globe "The Boston Globe")_ said "had ‘White Mischief’ been a work of fiction it would have required the collaboration of [Agatha Christie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agatha_Christie "Agatha Christie") and [P. G. Wodehouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P._G._Wodehouse "P. G. Wodehouse")."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-10) While researching the book Fox also collected information about [Beryl Markham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beryl_Markham "Beryl Markham"), which was turned into the film _[A Shadow on the Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beryl\_Markham:\_A\_Shadow\_on\_the\_Sun "Beryl Markham: A Shadow on the Sun")_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-11)

## Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Development")]

The film rights to the book were optioned by [Michael White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_White_(producer) "Michael White (producer)"), a friend of Fox's, while the book was being written.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-12)

Director Michael Radford collaborated with British playwright [Jonathan Gems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Gems "Jonathan Gems") on the script. Radford emphasized that "films of [Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa "Africa") should be made by Africans" and described the project as "a film of melancholy about people who have everything and yet have nothing. It's about people who want to possess what they can't possess."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-csm-13)

Securing funding for the film posed a challenge. The financing was sourced from a chain of Canadian cinemas, [Cineplex Odeon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cineplex_Odeon_Corporation "Cineplex Odeon Corporation"), plus [Goldcrest Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldcrest_Films "Goldcrest Films")[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-ink-14), BBC Television, [Nelson Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Entertainment "Nelson Entertainment") (headed by [Barry Spikings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Spikings "Barry Spikings"), which provided $2.5 million in exchange for North American video rights), with the remaining amount coming from [Columbia Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Pictures "Columbia Pictures"), then under [David Puttnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Puttnam "David Puttnam") as head of production.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-white-2)

[Richard Attenborough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Attenborough "Richard Attenborough") was offered and turned down the lead role, because he wanted to focus on directing films.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-15)

## Shooting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Shooting")]

Filming took place from February to May 1987 at [Shepperton Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shepperton_Studios "Shepperton Studios") and on location in Kenya.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-16)[Wrotham Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrotham_Park "Wrotham Park") was used as [Doddington Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doddington_Hall,_Cheshire "Doddington Hall, Cheshire"), the home of Delves Broughton.

## Historical accuracy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Historical accuracy")]

The real Alice De Janzé shot herself on 30 September 1941,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-17) while Jock Delves Broughton eventually returned to England and committed suicide by [morphine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphine "Morphine") overdose in the [Adelphi Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britannia_Adelphi_Hotel "Britannia Adelphi Hotel") in [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool "Liverpool") in December 1942, over a year later.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-18)

"There is a difference between fact and truth," said producer Simon Perry. "You can be truthful without being factual. It's inevitable there will be people who think Kenya was and still is a paradise of [remittance men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remittance_man "Remittance man") and black sheep of aristocratic families. Kenya was an exaggerated microcosm of society in Britain at that time, painted in primary colours with characters larger than life."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-csm-13)

Sir Jock Broughton's son, Sir Evelyn, complained that the film depicted his father as a murderer. He said his father was too drunk that night to have committed the crime and that Diana was more likely to have done it.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-19)

Diana Broughton died in 1987.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-20)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Box office

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Box office")]

The film grossed £1,532,903 in the United Kingdom and $3.1 million in the United States and Canada.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-screen-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-mojo-5) It lost money during its theatrical release, however, [Jake Eberts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Eberts "Jake Eberts") reported that [Goldcrest Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldcrest_Films "Goldcrest Films") invested £1,300,000 in the film, and received £1,633,000, earning them a profit of £333,000.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-screen-4)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-23)

### Critical

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Critical")]

_[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety\_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")_ wrote the film "displays high production values, impressive acting talent, and a strong — virtually factual — storyline. The money invested can be seen on the screen, and with an excellent lead performance (following his major role in ‘‘The Sicilian’’) Joss Ackland should finally receive the acting kudos he deserves. Pic should make a healthy b.o. impact worldwide."[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-24)

Book author James Fox said he was "ambivalent" about the movie.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-jongh-7)

Radford said the reviews of the film " almost ruined my career. It stopped it in its tracks... I think it was difficult for critics because Britain is obsessed by class. It wasn’t done to make a film about upper-class people. I think people were expecting one of those James Ivory films or _A Passage to India_... It wasn’t meant to be like _Out of Africa_, the cinema of waxed furniture. I was trying to make something much more decadent."[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-25)

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Legacy")]

In 1996, [Mariette Bosch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariette_Bosch "Mariette Bosch") murdered Ria Wolmerans in [Botswana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botswana "Botswana"). Both women were white South Africans. The case was referred to as "Botswana's white mischief".[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-BarrowBBC-26)

**Jonathan Gems** (born 1952, in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London")) is a British playwright and screenwriter mostly known for his work on _[Mars Attacks!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars\_Attacks! "Mars Attacks!")_ (1996), directed by [Tim Burton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Burton "Tim Burton").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Gems#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Gems#cite_note-2) He also wrote the film's [novelization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Novelization "Novelization"). His well known work includes a screenplay for an adaptation of [George Orwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Orwell "George Orwell")'s novel _[1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen\_Eighty-Four "Nineteen Eighty-Four")_ and _Mars Attacks Memoirs_, a book of interviews about working with Tim Burton behind the scenes of _Mars Attacks!_.

The son of the playwright [Pam Gems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pam_Gems "Pam Gems"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Gems#cite_note-3) Gems wrote a number of plays for theatres on the London fringe before gradually turning to screenwriting.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Gems#cite_note-4) As well as _Mars Attacks!_, Gems did uncredited rewrite work on _[Batman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman\_(1989\_film) "Batman (1989 film)")_ (1989). Gems has written unproduced scripts for Burton, including a _[Beetlejuice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beetlejuice "Beetlejuice")_ (1988) sequel titled _Beetlejuice Goes Hawaiian_; an updating of [Edgar Allan Poe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Allan_Poe "Edgar Allan Poe")'s "[The Fall of the House of Usher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fall_of_the_House_of_Usher "The Fall of the House of Usher")" set in [Burbank, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank,_California "Burbank, California"); _[The Hawkline Monster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hawkline\_Monster:\_A\_Gothic\_Western#Adaptations "The Hawkline Monster: A Gothic Western")_, a cowboy/monster movie that was to star [Clint Eastwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clint_Eastwood "Clint Eastwood") and [Jack Nicholson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Nicholson "Jack Nicholson"); and _Go Baby Go_, a beach movie in the style of films by [Russ Meyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russ_Meyer "Russ Meyer").

**Jonathan Gems** (born 1952, in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London")) is a British playwright and screenwriter mostly known for his work on _[Mars Attacks!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars\_Attacks! "Mars Attacks!")_ (1996), directed by [Tim Burton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Burton "Tim Burton").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Gems#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Gems#cite_note-2) He also wrote the film's [novelization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Novelization "Novelization"). His well known work includes a screenplay for an adaptation of [George Orwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Orwell "George Orwell")'s novel _[1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen\_Eighty-Four "Nineteen Eighty-Four")_ and _Mars Attacks Memoirs_, a book of interviews about working with Tim Burton behind the scenes of _Mars Attacks!_.

The son of the playwright [Pam Gems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pam_Gems "Pam Gems"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Gems#cite_note-3) Gems wrote a number of plays for theatres on the London fringe before gradually turning to screenwriting.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Gems#cite_note-4) As well as _Mars Attacks!_, Gems did uncredited rewrite work on _[Batman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman\_(1989\_film) "Batman (1989 film)")_ (1989). Gems has written unproduced scripts for Burton, including a _[Beetlejuice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beetlejuice "Beetlejuice")_ (1988) sequel titled _Beetlejuice Goes Hawaiian_; an updating of [Edgar Allan Poe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Allan_Poe "Edgar Allan Poe")'s "[The Fall of the House of Usher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fall_of_the_House_of_Usher "The Fall of the House of Usher")" set in [Burbank, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank,_California "Burbank, California"); _[The Hawkline Monster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hawkline\_Monster:\_A\_Gothic\_Western#Adaptations "The Hawkline Monster: A Gothic Western")_, a cowboy/monster movie that was to star [Clint Eastwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clint_Eastwood "Clint Eastwood") and [Jack Nicholson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Nicholson "Jack Nicholson"); and _Go Baby Go_, a beach movie in the style of films by [Russ Meyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russ_Meyer "Russ Meyer").

**James William Fox** (born **William Fox**; 19 May 1939) is an English actor, known for his work in film and television. He is a member of the [Fox family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Fox_family "Robin Fox family") of actors. Fox's career began in the 1960s through leading roles in films such as _[The Servant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Servant\_(1963\_film) "The Servant (1963 film)")_ (1963), _[King Rat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King\_Rat\_(film) "King Rat (film)")_ (1965), _[Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Those\_Magnificent\_Men\_in\_Their\_Flying\_Machines "Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines")_ (1965), _[Thoroughly Modern Millie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoroughly\_Modern\_Millie "Thoroughly Modern Millie")_ (1967), and _[Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance\_(film) "Performance (film)")_ (1970).

In the 1970s, Fox took a break from acting to focus on personal and spiritual matters, returning to acting in the early 1980s. Over time, he built a reputation for playing a variety of roles, including upper-class figures and more serious characters, notably in known for his roles in _[A Passage to India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Passage\_to\_India\_(film) "A Passage to India (film)")_ (1984), _[Patriot Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriot\_Games\_(film) "Patriot Games (film)")_ (1992), _[The Remains of the Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Remains\_of\_the\_Day\_(film) "The Remains of the Day (film)")_ (1993), _[Jinnah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jinnah\_(film) "Jinnah (film)")_ (1998), _[Sherlock Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherlock\_Holmes\_(2009\_film) "Sherlock Holmes (2009 film)")_ (2009), and _[Effie Gray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effie\_Gray\_(film) "Effie Gray (film)")_ (2014).

Fox won the [BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Most_Promising_Newcomer_to_Leading_Film_Roles "BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles") for his performance in _The Servant_, and was nominated for [Best Actor in a Supporting Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Supporting_Role "BAFTA Award for Best Actor in a Supporting Role") for _A Passage to India_. He is also a [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards") nominee.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

William Fox was born on 19 May 1939 in London, the second son of [theatrical agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatrical_agent "Theatrical agent")[Robin Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Fox_(theatrical_agent) "Robin Fox (theatrical agent)")[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-1) and actress Angela Worthington. His elder brother is actor [Edward Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Fox_(actor) "Edward Fox (actor)") and his younger brother was film producer [Robert Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Fox_(producer) "Robert Fox (producer)"). Fox's maternal grandfather was playwright [Frederick Lonsdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_Lonsdale "Frederick Lonsdale").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-foxes-2) He applied successfully to study acting at the [Central School of Speech and Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Central_School_of_Speech_and_Drama "Royal Central School of Speech and Drama").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-cssd-3)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early career")]

Fox first appeared on film as 11-year-old Toby Miniver in _[The Miniver Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Miniver\_Story "The Miniver Story")_ in 1950.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-acid-4) His early screen appearances, both in film and television, were made under his birth name, William Fox.

Fox appeared in the film _[The Loneliness of the Long Distance Runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Loneliness\_of\_the\_Long\_Distance\_Runner\_(film) "The Loneliness of the Long Distance Runner (film)")_ (1962).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) His father, [Robin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Fox_(theatrical_agent) "Robin Fox (theatrical agent)"), quarrelled bitterly with [Tony Richardson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Richardson "Tony Richardson") over this, having attempted to forbid his friend from giving his son James (known as "Willie") a part in the film. His father claimed Willie had no talent for acting and should not give up his job in a bank.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-6)

In 1964, Fox won a [BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Most_Promising_Newcomer_to_Leading_Film_Roles "BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles") for _[The Servant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Servant\_(1963\_film) "The Servant (1963 film)")_ (1963), working alongside [Dirk Bogarde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Bogarde "Dirk Bogarde"), [Sarah Miles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Miles "Sarah Miles"), and [Wendy Craig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendy_Craig "Wendy Craig").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-bafta-1964-7) On 16 June 1965, [Ken Annakin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Annakin "Ken Annakin")'s period aviation film _[Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Those\_Magnificent\_Men\_in\_Their\_Flying\_Machines "Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines")_ was released. In this British [period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Period_film "Period film")[comedy film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_film "Comedy film"), Fox is featured among an international [ensemble cast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ensemble_cast "Ensemble cast") including [Stuart Whitman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuart_Whitman "Stuart Whitman"), Sarah Miles, [Robert Morley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Morley "Robert Morley"), [Terry-Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry-Thomas "Terry-Thomas"), [Red Skelton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Skelton "Red Skelton"), [Benny Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benny_Hill "Benny Hill"), [Jean-Pierre Cassel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Pierre_Cassel "Jean-Pierre Cassel"), [Gert Fröbe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gert_Fr%C3%B6be "Gert Fröbe") and [Alberto Sordi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberto_Sordi "Alberto Sordi").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-nytimes_066838-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-variety_1200420712-9) Some of the other films he acted in during this time are _[King Rat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King\_Rat\_(film) "King Rat (film)")_ (1965),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_[The Chase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Chase\_(1966\_film) "The Chase (1966 film)")_ (1966),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_[Thoroughly Modern Millie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoroughly\_Modern\_Millie "Thoroughly Modern Millie")_ (1967),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_[Isadora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isadora\_(film) "Isadora (film)")_ (1968),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) and _[Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance\_(film) "Performance (film)")_ (1970).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-acid-4)

### Spiritual life and break from acting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Spiritual life and break from acting")]

After finishing work on _[Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance\_(film) "Performance (film)")_ (released 1970, but shot in 1968),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) Fox suspended his acting career. The film, which starred Fox and [Mick Jagger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Jagger "Mick Jagger"), was deemed so outrageous that critics at a preview screening walked out, with one film executive's wife reportedly throwing up in the cinema.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-acid-4)

In a 2008 interview, Fox said: "It was just part of my journey...I think my journey was to spend a while away from acting. And I never lost contact with it – watching movies, reading about it ... so I didn't feel I missed it."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tweed-10)

Fox became an evangelical Christian, working with the [Navigators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Navigators_(organization) "The Navigators (organization)") and devoting himself to the ministry.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-cinema-11) During this time, the only film in which Fox appeared was _No Longer Alone_ (1976), the story of Joan Winmill Brown,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-epit-12) a suicidal woman who was led to faith in [Jesus Christ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus_Christ "Jesus Christ") by [Ruth Bell Graham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruth_Bell_Graham "Ruth Bell Graham").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-epit-12)

### Return to acting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Return to acting")]

After an absence from acting of several years, in 1981 Fox appeared on television in the _[Play for Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Play\_for\_Today "Play for Today")_ "Country" by [Trevor Griffiths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Griffiths "Trevor Griffiths"), a comedy drama set against the 1945 UK parliamentary elections. On film he starred in [Stephen Poliakoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Poliakoff "Stephen Poliakoff")'s _[Runners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runners\_(film) "Runners (film)")_ (1983),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_[A Passage to India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Passage\_to\_India\_(film) "A Passage to India (film)")_ (1984),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) and _[Comrades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comrades\_(1986\_film) "Comrades (1986 film)")_ (1986).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) He played [Anthony Blunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Blunt "Anthony Blunt") in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") play by [Alan Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Bennett "Alan Bennett"), _[A Question of Attribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Question\_of\_Attribution "A Question of Attribution")_ (1992).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) He also portrayed the character of Lord Holmes in _[Patriot Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriot\_Games "Patriot Games")_ (1992), as well as Colonel Ferguson in _[Farewell to the King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farewell\_to\_the\_King "Farewell to the King")_ (1989) and the Nazi-sympathising aristocrat Lord Darlington in _[The Remains of the Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Remains\_of\_the\_Day\_(film) "The Remains of the Day (film)")_ (1993).

Fox has since appeared in the 2000 film _[Sexy Beast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexy\_Beast\_(film) "Sexy Beast (film)")_,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) the [2001 adaptation of _The Lost World_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lost_World_(2001_film) "The Lost World (2001 film)") as Prof. Leo Summerlee,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_[Agatha Christie's Poirot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agatha\_Christie's\_Poirot "Agatha Christie's Poirot") – [Death on the ## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Fox married Mary Elizabeth Piper in September 1973, with whom he has five children, including [Laurence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Fox "Laurence Fox") and [Jack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Fox_(actor) "Jack Fox (actor)"). Piper died at their home on 19 April 2020.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-foxes-2)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-telegraph_241195-15)

Through his daughter Lydia, Fox's son-in-law is actor [Richard Ayoade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Ayoade "Richard Ayoade").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-telegraph_20170623-16) His former daughter-in-law is actress [Billie Piper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Piper "Billie Piper"), who was married to his son Laurence from 2007 to 2016.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-BBC_News-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-itv_20160512-18)
