**James William Fox** (born **William Fox**; 19 May 1939) is an English actor, known for his work in film and television. He is a member of the [Fox family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Fox_family "Robin Fox family") of actors. Fox's career began in the 1960s through leading roles in films such as _[The Servant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Servant\_(1963\_film) "The Servant (1963 film)")_ (1963), _[King Rat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King\_Rat\_(film) "King Rat (film)")_ (1965), _[Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Those\_Magnificent\_Men\_in\_Their\_Flying\_Machines "Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines")_ (1965), _[Thoroughly Modern Millie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoroughly\_Modern\_Millie "Thoroughly Modern Millie")_ (1967), and _[Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance\_(film) "Performance (film)")_ (1970).

In the 1970s, Fox took a break from acting to focus on personal and spiritual matters, returning to acting in the early 1980s. Over time, he built a reputation for playing a variety of roles, including upper-class figures and more serious characters, notably in known for his roles in _[A Passage to India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Passage\_to\_India\_(film) "A Passage to India (film)")_ (1984), _[Patriot Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriot\_Games\_(film) "Patriot Games (film)")_ (1992), _[The Remains of the Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Remains\_of\_the\_Day\_(film) "The Remains of the Day (film)")_ (1993), _[Jinnah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jinnah\_(film) "Jinnah (film)")_ (1998), _[Sherlock Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherlock\_Holmes\_(2009\_film) "Sherlock Holmes (2009 film)")_ (2009), and _[Effie Gray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effie\_Gray\_(film) "Effie Gray (film)")_ (2014).

Fox won the [BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Most_Promising_Newcomer_to_Leading_Film_Roles "BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles") for his performance in _The Servant_, and was nominated for [Best Actor in a Supporting Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Supporting_Role "BAFTA Award for Best Actor in a Supporting Role") for _A Passage to India_. He is also a [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards") nominee.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

William Fox was born on 19 May 1939 in London, the second son of [theatrical agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatrical_agent "Theatrical agent")[Robin Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Fox_(theatrical_agent) "Robin Fox (theatrical agent)")[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-1) and actress Angela Worthington. His elder brother is actor [Edward Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Fox_(actor) "Edward Fox (actor)") and his younger brother was film producer [Robert Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Fox_(producer) "Robert Fox (producer)"). Fox's maternal grandfather was playwright [Frederick Lonsdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_Lonsdale "Frederick Lonsdale").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-foxes-2) He applied successfully to study acting at the [Central School of Speech and Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Central_School_of_Speech_and_Drama "Royal Central School of Speech and Drama").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-cssd-3)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early career")]

Fox first appeared on film as 11-year-old Toby Miniver in _[The Miniver Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Miniver\_Story "The Miniver Story")_ in 1950.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-acid-4) His early screen appearances, both in film and television, were made under his birth name, William Fox.

Fox appeared in the film _[The Loneliness of the Long Distance Runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Loneliness\_of\_the\_Long\_Distance\_Runner\_(film) "The Loneliness of the Long Distance Runner (film)")_ (1962).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) His father, [Robin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Fox_(theatrical_agent) "Robin Fox (theatrical agent)"), quarrelled bitterly with [Tony Richardson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Richardson "Tony Richardson") over this, having attempted to forbid his friend from giving his son James (known as "Willie") a part in the film. His father claimed Willie had no talent for acting and should not give up his job in a bank.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-6)

In 1964, Fox won a [BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Most_Promising_Newcomer_to_Leading_Film_Roles "BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles") for _[The Servant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Servant\_(1963\_film) "The Servant (1963 film)")_ (1963), working alongside [Dirk Bogarde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Bogarde "Dirk Bogarde"), [Sarah Miles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Miles "Sarah Miles"), and [Wendy Craig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendy_Craig "Wendy Craig").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-bafta-1964-7) On 16 June 1965, [Ken Annakin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Annakin "Ken Annakin")'s period aviation film _[Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Those\_Magnificent\_Men\_in\_Their\_Flying\_Machines "Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines")_ was released. In this British [period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Period_film "Period film")[comedy film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_film "Comedy film"), Fox is featured among an international [ensemble cast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ensemble_cast "Ensemble cast") including [Stuart Whitman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuart_Whitman "Stuart Whitman"), Sarah Miles, [Robert Morley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Morley "Robert Morley"), [Terry-Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry-Thomas "Terry-Thomas"), [Red Skelton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Skelton "Red Skelton"), [Benny Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benny_Hill "Benny Hill"), [Jean-Pierre Cassel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Pierre_Cassel "Jean-Pierre Cassel"), [Gert Fröbe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gert_Fr%C3%B6be "Gert Fröbe") and [Alberto Sordi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberto_Sordi "Alberto Sordi").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-nytimes_066838-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-variety_1200420712-9) Some of the other films he acted in during this time are _[King Rat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King\_Rat\_(film) "King Rat (film)")_ (1965),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_[The Chase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Chase\_(1966\_film) "The Chase (1966 film)")_ (1966),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_[Thoroughly Modern Millie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoroughly\_Modern\_Millie "Thoroughly Modern Millie")_ (1967),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_[Isadora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isadora\_(film) "Isadora (film)")_ (1968),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) and _[Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance\_(film) "Performance (film)")_ (1970).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-acid-4)

### Spiritual life and break from acting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Spiritual life and break from acting")]

After finishing work on _[Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance\_(film) "Performance (film)")_ (released 1970, but shot in 1968),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) Fox suspended his acting career. The film, which starred Fox and [Mick Jagger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Jagger "Mick Jagger"), was deemed so outrageous that critics at a preview screening walked out, with one film executive's wife reportedly throwing up in the cinema.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-acid-4)

In a 2008 interview, Fox said: "It was just part of my journey...I think my journey was to spend a while away from acting. And I never lost contact with it – watching movies, reading about it ... so I didn't feel I missed it."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tweed-10)

Fox became an evangelical Christian, working with the [Navigators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Navigators_(organization) "The Navigators (organization)") and devoting himself to the ministry.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-cinema-11) During this time, the only film in which Fox appeared was _No Longer Alone_ (1976), the story of Joan Winmill Brown,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-epit-12) a suicidal woman who was led to faith in [Jesus Christ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus_Christ "Jesus Christ") by [Ruth Bell Graham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruth_Bell_Graham "Ruth Bell Graham").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-epit-12)

### Return to acting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Return to acting")]

After an absence from acting of several years, in 1981 Fox appeared on television in the _[Play for Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Play\_for\_Today "Play for Today")_ "Country" by [Trevor Griffiths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Griffiths "Trevor Griffiths"), a comedy drama set against the 1945 UK parliamentary elections. On film he starred in [Stephen Poliakoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Poliakoff "Stephen Poliakoff")'s _[Runners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runners\_(film) "Runners (film)")_ (1983),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_[A Passage to India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Passage\_to\_India\_(film) "A Passage to India (film)")_ (1984),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) and _[Comrades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comrades\_(1986\_film) "Comrades (1986 film)")_ (1986).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) He played [Anthony Blunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Blunt "Anthony Blunt") in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") play by [Alan Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Bennett "Alan Bennett"), _[A Question of Attribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Question\_of\_Attribution "A Question of Attribution")_ (1992).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) He also portrayed the character of Lord Holmes in _[Patriot Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriot\_Games "Patriot Games")_ (1992), as well as Colonel Ferguson in _[Farewell to the King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farewell\_to\_the\_King "Farewell to the King")_ (1989) and the Nazi-sympathising aristocrat Lord Darlington in _[The Remains of the Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Remains\_of\_the\_Day\_(film) "The Remains of the Day (film)")_ (1993).

Fox has since appeared in the 2000 film _[Sexy Beast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexy\_Beast\_(film) "Sexy Beast (film)")_,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) the [2001 adaptation of _The Lost World_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lost_World_(2001_film) "The Lost World (2001 film)") as Prof. Leo ## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Fox married Mary Elizabeth Piper in September 1973, with whom he has five children, including [Laurence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Fox "Laurence Fox") and [Jack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Fox_(actor) "Jack Fox (actor)"). Piper died at their home on 19 April 2020.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-foxes-2)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-telegraph_241195-15)

Through his daughter Lydia, Fox's son-in-law is actor [Richard Ayoade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Ayoade "Richard Ayoade").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-telegraph_20170623-16) His former daughter-in-law is actress [Billie Piper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Piper "Billie Piper"), who was married to his son Laurence from 2007 to 2016.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-BBC_News-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-itv_20160512-18)
